resources.string: Shows a daily verse from the Tao Te Ching.
The Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao;\nthe name that can be named is not the constant name.
Highest goodness is like water.\nWater excels in benefiting all things without striving.
Thirty spokes share one hub;\nit is in its emptiness that the usefulness of the cart lies.
Yield and remain whole;\nbend and be straightened;\nempty and be filled.
To speak sparingly is natural.\nA whirlwind does not last all morning;\na sudden downpour does not last all day.
The heavy is the root of the light;\nthe calm is the master of the hasty.
Return is the movement of the Dao.\nYielding is the way of the Dao.
When a wise person hears of the Dao, they practice it diligently.
He who knows when he has enough is rich.\nHe who knows when to stop is free from danger.
Those who know do not speak;\nthose who speak do not know.
Act without acting;\nwork without working;\ntaste without tasting.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
I have three treasures:\ncompassion, frugality, and humility.
True words are not beautiful;\nbeautiful words are not true.
